issues.failure_explanation: The abstract states that F is the largest set of measures for which 'any measure-dependent affine transport' could be exact and concludes that the EnKU is near-optimal 'among affine transports'. Definition def:affine_cond_map allows A, B, c to depend on both pi and y_star, but F is defined and Theorem thm:F_char is proved only for weakly y_star-dependent maps (A(pi), B(pi) independent of y_star). Section 3.2 itself exhibits fully y_star-dependent affine conditioning maps (e.g. L_{y_star}(x,y)=f(y_star)y for pi=phi_sharp(r⊗r)) that are exact for measures outside F, so the exact set of a general affine conditioning map is not contained in E^EnKU ∪ S_nl-dec. The abstract/Section 4 statements therefore assert an optimality that the formal results do not establish and that the paper's own examples refute.

failure_location.quote: Finally, we ask what the largest possible set of measures  \(\mathrm{F}\) is that any measure-dependent affine transport could be exact for.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the prose claims to weakly y_star-dependent affine conditioning maps (A and B independent of y_star), matching the definition of F and the statement of Theorem thm:F_char, and explicitly note in the abstract that fully y_star-dependent maps can have strictly larger exact sets.
issues.overall_effect: The headline near-optimality/uniqueness-of-exactness claims in the abstract, the phrase 'any other affine conditioning map' in the introduction, and the Section 4 claim that the EnKU is 'the only method that remains exact beyond highly symmetric laws' are unsupported for the general class of affine conditioning maps; they hold only for the weakly y_star-dependent subclass. Formal results (Theorems thm:enkf_update_unique, thm:F_char, Corollary cor:enkf_char) are unaffected.
issues.title: Abstract/introduction claim near-optimality of the EnKU among all measure-dependent affine transports, but the result only covers weakly y*-dependent maps and the paper's own examples contradict the broader claim
issues.why_classification: No formal result needs changing, but the advertised optimality claim over all affine transports is false as stated and must be withdrawn to the weakly y_star-dependent subclass, a material narrowing of the paper's stated scope rather than a cosmetic fix.
